security_concerns: P2 — docs/PERFORMANCE.md:33 and contracts/failure-fixtures.json:10 claim content cannot enter storage 'by schema', but docs/PROTOCOL.md:11-12,42 permits opaque string identifiers and adapter-version metadata. Excluding prompt/response field names does not prevent an erroneous adapter from placing sensitive text in these accepted strings. This overstates the privacy guarantee and could justify persisting contaminated metadata. Describe field-level minimization rather than content impossibility, and require adapter provenance/mapping checks and canary tests before persistence. This is a documentation-contract issue, not evidence of an implemented leak.
logic_errors: P2 — scripts/verify-m0.py:12-26 never checks the fixture schema_version declared in contracts/failure-fixtures.json:2. Independently tested mutations setting schema_version to 999 or removing it both returned an empty error list. Consequently the checker reports success for an unsupported or unversioned fixture format rather than detecting incompatible contract artifacts. Require the supported integer schema version and add negative tests.
suggestions: scripts/verify-m0.py:14-20,30 — Validate container and ID types before calling get() or constructing sets, and convert expected input/file errors into the existing JSON error output. In-memory tests with a list root, a null scenario, and a list-valued ID raised AttributeError/TypeError. These fail nonzero rather than falsely passing, but callers lose structured diagnostics.

scripts/verify-m0.py:7-9 and tests/test_m0_contracts.py:21-42 — Explicitly document whether the additional scenarios are optional, or protect their presence too. Removing all seven scenarios outside REQUIRED still passed validation, so accidental deletion of wrong-target, launch-retry, slow-consumer and other currently documented cases is not detected.

docs/PERFORMANCE.md:34 and docs/PROTOCOL.md:52 — Define the relationship between bounded tombstone retention and late-event rejection before M1 implementation. Specify when a generation is retired or reconciliation becomes mandatory after tombstone eviction; otherwise implementers can choose pruning behavior that allows an old terminal turn to reappear as working.
summary: Reviewed all eight staged files read-only and independently confirmed the static scan found no secret assignments, shell=True/os.system, eval/exec, unsafe pickle, or dangerous permission patterns. The fixture checker and both unit tests passed; targeted mutations exposed the schema-version validation gap. Same-UID limitations, pending licensing, and the distinction between synthetic requirements and measured performance are otherwise explicit. No files were created or modified; no production performance or harness integration was verified.
